findings.title: SQL injection authentication bypass
findings.summary: Logged in as the first registered user (admin) by injecting `' OR 1=1--` into the email field, bypassing the password check.

findings.title: SQL injection & verbose error leak in product search
findings.summary: The /rest/products/search endpoint concatenates the `q` param into SQL and returns the raw SQLite error, confirming injection.

findings.title: Confidential document exposed via static file route
findings.summary: Retrieved an internal confidential document from /ftp with no authentication or authorisation required.

findings.title: Missing HTTP security headers
findings.summary: Response is served without Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options.

findings.title: Application version disclosure
findings.summary: An unauthenticated endpoint returns the exact application version, letting an attacker match it to known CVEs.

remediations.title: Parameterise the login query
remediations.rationale: The bypass works because user input is concatenated into SQL. Parameterised queries send the input as data, never as code, so `' OR 1=1--` is treated as a (nonexistent) email, not as syntax.
remediations.code_fix_before:
const q = `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email}' AND password = '${hash(req.body.password)}'`;
db.exec(q);

remediations.title: Parameterise search + return a generic error
remediations.rationale: Two fixes: bind the query parameter so the quote can't break the SQL, and replace the raw DB error with a generic 400 so the engine and schema aren't leaked to the client.
remediations.code_fix_before:
const q = `SELECT * FROM Products WHERE name LIKE '%${req.query.q}%'`;
// ... catch (e) { res.status(500).send(e.toString()); }
remediations.code_fix_after:
db.all('SELECT * FROM Products WHERE name LIKE ?', [`%${q}%`])
// ... catch (e) { log.error(e); res.status(400).json({error:'Invalid query'}); }

remediations.title: Gate the /ftp route behind auth + an allow-list
remediations.rationale: Static internal files are served with no check. Require authentication for the route and only serve an explicit allow-list of public file types.

remediations.title: Add Helmet security headers
remediations.rationale: A single middleware sets Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, HSTS and X-Content-Type-Options — closing off XSS, clickjacking and downgrade attacks at once.

remediations.title: Stop publishing the exact version
remediations.rationale: Fingerprinting the version maps the app to known CVEs. Remove the public version endpoint (or return a static build id) and patch on a schedule rather than relying on obscurity.
remediations.code_fix_after:
// endpoint removed from public surface; version tracked internally
// in the SBOM / dependency scanner, not exposed to clients
